hints.title: Track Min and Max
hints.text: Because matrix contains negative numbers, a negative multiplied by a negative becomes positive.

hints.title: Grid DP State
hints.text: For each cell, maintain both the maximum and minimum reachable products from the start.

hints.title: Modulo at the End
hints.text: Do not take modulo during intermediate multiplications to preserve correct comparisons.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxProductPath(self, grid: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        m, n = len(grid), len(grid[0])
        dp_max = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
        dp_min = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
        dp_max[0][0] = dp_min[0][0] = grid[0][0]
        for r in range(1, m):
            dp_max[r][0] = dp_min[r][0] = dp_max[r-1][0] * grid[r][0]
        for c in range(1, n):
            dp_max[0][c] = dp_min[0][c] = dp_max[0][c-1] * grid[0][c]
        for r in range(1, m):
            for c in range(1, n):
                val = grid[r][c]
                cands = [
                    dp_max[r-1][c] * val, dp_min[r-1][c] * val,
                    dp_max[r][c-1] * val, dp_min[r][c-1] * val
                ]
                dp_max[r][c] = max(cands)
                dp_min[r][c] = min(cands)
        ans = dp_max[m-1][n-1]
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        return ans % MOD if ans >= 0 else -1
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Tracking only the maximum product fails because multiplying a large negative product with a negative number creates a new maximum.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual DP matrices track min and max simultaneously in O(m * n) time and space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should understand why intermediate modulo cannot be applied when comparing values.
